lesson.title: Opa Distance

sections.title: Understanding Opa Units
sections.content: One opa unit is a measure of distance. According to the text, one opa unit equals four metres (Section 1).

sections.title: Calculating Distance
sections.content:
To find the total distance for multiple units, we multiply the number of units by the length of one unit.

Calculation:
9 units × 4 metres per unit = 36 metres.

The text confirms that nine units measure thirty-six metres (Section 1).

lesson.title: Understanding One Third

sections.title: What is One Third?
sections.content: One third means one of three equal parts of a whole group. To be 'equal' means each part has the same number.

sections.title: Example: Sharing Apples
sections.content: If you have 12 apples and share them among 3 people, each person gets 4 apples. In this group of 12, the 4 apples given to one person represent one third.

lesson.summary: One third is one equal part out of three total parts. For example, if 12 apples are shared equally by 3 people, each person gets 4 apples.
discussion_questions: If three people share twelve apples equally, how many apples does each person get?
objectives: Explain one third in simple words
lesson.content:
One third means one of three equal parts of a whole group. To be 'equal' means each part has the same number.

If you have 12 apples and share them among 3 people, each person gets 4 apples. In this group of 12, the 4 apples given to one person represent one third.

exercises.question: How many total tokens are there in all four rema bags?
exercises.explanation: According to the source data, there are four rema bags and each bag contains nine tokens. To find the total, you multiply 4 (bags) by 9 (tokens per bag), which equals 36.
hints: Think about how many tokens are in just one bag.
If one bag has 9 tokens, how many would be in two bags?
Multiply the number of bags by the number of tokens in each bag.
